rules.rule: Dense dispatch can use a bounds check and a CS-relative jump table.
rules.trigger: Several distinct targets in a compact value range.
rules.source_form: switch (hittype[i][0]) with four distinct arms.
rules.emitted_code: CMP selector,3; JA default; JMP CS:[selector*4+table]. A nonzero first case adds an index bias.
rules.counter_example: The DOS fixture with three contiguous cases used comparisons in all four profiles. Four contiguous cases used tables in all four.
rules.reference: probes.json / sw_3_1 and sw_4_1

rules.rule: Case density and the optimization profile influence dispatch selection.
rules.trigger: Distinct cases with identical arm structure, all calling separate external functions, and the same external default.
rules.source_form: switch (x) with cases 100 + i*step for i=0 through n-1.
rules.emitted_code: For stride 2, only n=4 used a table in engine/multi. game_oe/audiolib used tables for n=4,5,6,8,10,16. For stride 3, only game_oe/audiolib n=4,5 used tables. All stride 4,8,16 fixtures used comparisons.
rules.counter_example: At stride 2, n=12 uses a comparison tree in all profiles. There is no monotone case-count threshold in this fixture.
rules.reference: probes.json / case_matrix

rules.rule: Compare trees retain the selector width and can encode adjacent labels as a range.
rules.trigger: Case selector can remain in a narrow live value, and contiguous case labels share a body.
rules.source_form: switch (tempbuf[0]); switch (wall[i].picnum).
rules.emitted_code: CMP AL in getpackets. CMP AX plus JB/JBE around a contiguous case range in animatewalls.
rules.counter_example: parsecommand uses a word bounds test followed by a long index into a dispatch table.
rules.reference: docs/FINDINGS.md / Game code-shape rules and SECTOR round 3

rules.rule: Keep labels with empty bodies when reconstructing a compare tree.
rules.trigger: A label falls through into a shared body, or shares the default destination.
rules.source_form: case 1: case 7: ... in moveeffectors. Group actual empty and contiguous labels.
rules.emitted_code: Changing the case-value set changes the split keys and block order even when the high-level effect is unchanged for tested inputs.
rules.counter_example: The specific 1/7 split at 15 is local evidence from the still-NEAR moveeffectors.
rules.reference: docs/FINDINGS.md / GAME inlining structure

rules.rule: Switch tables can precede the entry label in CODE.
rules.trigger: An indexed indirect jump has a relocated intra-segment table base.
rules.source_form: A dense switch with distinct case bodies.
rules.emitted_code: Relocated dwords, then entry alignment padding, then the dispatcher public. Some Watcom 10.0 slots relocate to external tail callees.
rules.counter_example: Comparison trees have no such prefix. A table with external targets can remain inside the preceding public’s verified extent under the current verifier attribution rule.
rules.reference: docs/FINDINGS.md / Jump-table attribution in the verifier

rules.rule: A signed byte or word can extend directly into a long.
rules.trigger: An 8- or 16-bit signed memory value is needed as a 32-bit operand under -4r.
rules.source_form: (long)sprite[i].sectnum; klabs(ps[snum].look_ang).
rules.emitted_code: MOVSX r32,m16, or MOV AX,m16 followed by CWDE in the EAX-specific pragma path. The signed-byte fixture used MOVSX r32,m8.
rules.counter_example: The signed global -5r fixtures may read a dword at a negative addend and shift instead.
rules.reference: docs/FINDINGS.md / Allocator lever and MULTI; probes.json / widenschar and widensshort

rules.rule: Some -5r signed extensions use a wider, negatively displaced memory read.
rules.trigger: Promoting a signed narrow global. Watch for a relocation to an adjacent symbol or symbol plus a negative addend.
rules.source_form: i < numplayers - 1 with a signed-short numplayers. Fixture returns a signed char or short as long.
rules.emitted_code: MOV r32,[short-2]; SAR r32,16. The signed-byte fixture uses [char-3] and SAR r32,24.
rules.counter_example: A volatile short in the same -5r fixture used MOVSX directly. Several ordinary loads in the same modules also use MOVSX.
rules.reference: docs/FINDINGS.md / MULTI is compiled with -5r; probes.json / widenvolatile

rules.rule: Zeroing a register followed by a low-byte or low-word load is a promotion idiom.
rules.trigger: An unsigned narrow load must supply a zero-extended long.
rules.source_form: Unsigned char synctics or key byte used in a wide call/expression.
rules.emitted_code: XOR EAX,EAX; MOV AL,[synctics]. A word uses AX in the fixture. Other allocations can use MOVZX.
rules.counter_example: Multiple uses, preload timing, and inlining can favor AND r32,255 or a MOVZX instead.
rules.reference: probes.json / widenuchar, widenushort; corpus timerhandler inlined calls

rules.rule: An int-promoted expression can still compare at byte or word width.
rules.trigger: The optimizer can establish that a narrow operand and bound fit the required comparison.
rules.source_form: sprite[i].picnum == MASTERSWITCH; sprite[i].yvel == 0; totalclock & 16.
rules.emitted_code: CMP m16,imm or CMP r16,m16. A low-bit mask on a long can become TEST m8,imm8.
rules.counter_example: The same record’s long dimensionmode compares with CMP m32,imm. A cast or declaration affects the usable width.
rules.reference: docs/FINDINGS.md / Game code-shape rules

rules.rule: Check replaced enums during a narrow comparison mismatch.
rules.trigger: A narrow game expression is compared against a named enum constant or macro literal.
rules.source_form: Use the byte/short comparison from the recorded PLAYER/GAMEDEF controls to choose between declarations.
rules.emitted_code: The recorded controls changed 32-bit comparisons back to 16-bit comparisons or byte tests with literal macros.
rules.counter_example: A global signed-short return expression ss == 5 and ss == enum_five generate the same CMP word and even alias to one entry in all four fixtures.
rules.reference: docs/FINDINGS.md / Game code-shape rules; probes.json / cmpliteral versus cmpenum

rules.rule: A narrow result can pull the arithmetic itself down to word width.
rules.trigger: Inputs are long, but only the low word survives the explicit conversion.
rules.source_form: i = (short)(totalclock - lockclock);
rules.emitted_code: MOV AX,word [totalclock]; SUB AX,word [lockclock].
rules.counter_example: A full-width relational use reads and compares dwords, as in playback’s clock wait.
rules.reference: STRICT source and operand widths in index

rules.rule: Signed division by a power of two includes a correction toward zero.
rules.trigger: A signed 32-bit dividend can be negative, divisor is a positive power of two.
rules.source_form: ((long)menu_y - m.y) / 16 + 1.
rules.emitted_code: Copy dividend to r, SAR r,31; SHL r,4; SBB dividend,r; SAR dividend,4. The +1 remains an INC.
rules.counter_example: Unsigned /16 used one SHR r,4 in all four fixtures. Signed division by 9 used IDIV.
rules.reference: probes.json / signed16 and unsigned16

rules.rule: Small non-power-of-two constants can retain hardware division.
rules.trigger: A genuinely variable signed long dividend divided by 5, 9 or 20 in the indexed contexts.
rules.source_form: ni = n / 5; klabs(ps[snum].look_ang) / 9.
rules.emitted_code: Prepare EDX with SAR 31, load the divisor in a register, then IDIV. The unsigned fixture clears EDX and uses DIV.
rules.counter_example: (4 * 9 + 2) / 2 folds to MOV EAX,19. A /16 uses a shift sequence.
rules.reference: probes.json / signed9, unsigned9 and folded

rules.rule: Some constant products become shift plus add or subtract.
rules.trigger: A 32-bit product by a constant one away from a power of two.
rules.source_form: zvel = (...) * 31; offs = (x + 1) * (LAVASIZ + 2) + 1;
rules.emitted_code: Copy the input, shift left 5 then subtract the input for 31. In movelava, shift left 6 and add the input to get 65*x, then double for the product by 130. The final doubling appears under the next source line anchor.
rules.counter_example: The -4r fixture multiplies by 38 with IMUL. Under both -5r profiles the scalar *38 fixture uses shifts, adds and subtraction.
rules.reference: probes.json / times31, times65 and times38

rules.rule: Packed records of different sizes produce distinct index arithmetic.
rules.trigger: The map v5 layout uses sprite/wall/sector strides of 38/35/37. The game player record uses stride 240.
rules.source_form: sprite[i]; wall[i]; sector[sprite[i].sectnum]; ps[p].
rules.emitted_code: Sprite stride 38 often IMUL imm 0x26. Wall stride 35 is 9*i then 4*(9*i)-i. Sector stride 37 is 9*i then 4*(9*i)+i. Player stride 240 is 15*i shifted by 4.
rules.counter_example: A saved pointer, induction variable, or direct SIB scale (e.g. sintable[index*2]) changes what remains at each access.
rules.reference: STRICT normalized index and src/game/records.h

rules.rule: A constant subexpression can disappear into an earlier immediate load.
rules.trigger: All operands of a parenthesized subexpression are compile-time constants.
rules.emitted_code: MOV EAX,0x08000000 before the variable division. MOV EAX,0x00a00000 for the draw argument.
rules.counter_example: The variable division still emits IDIV. The calcwalls immediate is moved across the previous statement’s debug anchor.
rules.reference: STRICT index; probes.json / folded

rules.rule: Short-circuit operands commonly occupy separate conditional branches in source order.
rules.trigger: The next operand is evaluated only when the previous operand’s condition permits it.
rules.source_form: sprite[i].picnum == MASTERSWITCH && sprite[i].lotag == low && sprite[i].yvel == 0; flags joined by ||.
rules.emitted_code: Three CMP/JNE pairs for the && guard. A nonzero first operand jumps over the second load for || in BLASTER_BeginBufferedPlayback.
rules.counter_example: Pure operands or simple Boolean results can compile differently. Branch inversion in blockdiff hides polarity, so check symbolic assembly.
rules.reference: STRICT index; probes.json / andalso and orelse

rules.rule: SETcc materializes a Boolean in a low byte, with widening only where required.
rules.trigger: A comparison is used as a value by the caller or enclosing arithmetic.
rules.source_form: return strget(...) != 0; ((xvect < 0) << 10).
rules.emitted_code: SETNE AL for the narrow result. SETL AL, AND EAX,255, SHL EAX,10 for an arithmetic use.
rules.counter_example: A branch consumes the flags without SETcc. The ternary fixture plain ? 1 : 0 uses SETNE, whereas plain ? 11 : 22 uses separate branches and immediate loads.
rules.reference: STRICT index; probes.json / ternfold and ternconst

rules.rule: Top-tested source can preserve a loop’s early exit and bottom recheck.
rules.trigger: A list index is initialized before a while loop and tested before dereference.
rules.source_form: while (k >= 0) or j = 1; while (j < length).
rules.emitted_code: A zero-iteration edge before the first traversal and a conditional recheck leading toward the body.
rules.counter_example: Standalone checkhitswitch variants were identical while the inline layout in checksectors changed. A while can also have a bottom physical test after a jump from the entry.
rules.reference: docs/FINDINGS.md / SECTOR round 3, Other game units round 4 and MULTI is compiled with -5r

rules.rule: Identical return paths can share an epilogue across functions.
rules.trigger: A compatible save set, frame, and value state permit reuse of a neighbouring tail.
rules.source_form: Distinct `return` statements or simple functions with an identical terminal sequence.
rules.emitted_code: The later routine can JMP into the earlier return or restore sequence. Entire identical fixture bodies can have two publics at one offset.
rules.counter_example: A differing stack frame, live register or branch position can prevent sharing. A neighbour that changes size can break a STRICT function’s shared jump displacement.
rules.reference: docs/FINDINGS.md / Engine round 4; probes.json / cmpliteral and cmpenum

rules.rule: Identical blocks can be merged into a sibling that falls through to the common join.
rules.trigger: Two interchangeable blocks join the same successor and at least one falls through.
rules.source_form: Repeated update_menu_cursor(614); break; tails in switch arms.
rules.emitted_code: A merge leaves one block. With two explicit outgoing jumps both identical blocks survived the recorded mini test.
rules.counter_example: The suspected shared paths in processinput existed in both builds, so this rule did not explain its 184-byte size deficit.
rules.reference: docs/FINDINGS.md / Other game units round 4 and PLAYER and SECTOR round 5

rules.rule: Separate stores can fix emitted store order and remain distinct if their values coincide.
rules.trigger: Multiple stores have equal values or are adjacent in a branch.
rules.source_form: syncvel[snum] = 0; syncsvel[snum] = 0; syncangvel[snum] = 0;
rules.emitted_code: Three stores in the order in getinput. The same value can be shared in a register.
rules.counter_example: The recorded chained-assignment rewrite changes bytes. resetplayer needed a separate order for equal-valued stores.
rules.reference: docs/FINDINGS.md / GAME findings, PLAYER/ACTORS/MENUES round 2 and PREMAP/GAME round 3

rules.rule: A basic-block boundary can retain a memory read-modify-write.
rules.trigger: A memory update is followed by a branch or an inlined body that can affect scheduling.
rules.source_form: reccnt--; do { if (...) ... else ... } while (0); or totalclock++ before keytimerstuff().
rules.emitted_code: SUB [reccnt],EDX or INC [totalclock] survives. Inline expansion starts a new basic block in the recorded timer probe.
rules.counter_example: Removing the do/while in closedemowrite splits the update and adds 16 bytes. reccnt-- in playback has a register load at its debug anchor.
rules.reference: docs/FINDINGS.md / Inliner facts and GAME NEAR round 2

rules.rule: -oe=N applies a per-callee expression-tree budget.
rules.trigger: Same translation unit, callee eligible for user-function inlining. A forward definition is eligible.
rules.source_form: Natural calls under -4r -s -otexan -oe=3000.
rules.emitted_code: Plain -oe used N=20 in the recorded controls. N >=2500 fits the GAME call/inline pattern. Unit floors from oeunits were MENUES >=90, PLAYER >=485, SECTOR roughly >=1520, GAMEDEF roughly >=1330.
rules.counter_example: ENGINE has no -oe and all 181 intra-engine calls match. One ACTORS addweapon site needs the integrated comma-expression spelling at N=3000.
rules.reference: docs/FINDINGS.md / GAME’s inlining is real compiler inlining, All game units and Engine compiled without inlining

rules.rule: Inline expansion is one level deep in the recorded cases, including recursive callees.
rules.trigger: An otherwise eligible same-unit call under -oe=N.
rules.source_form: An eligible caller contains a call to getpackets or a recursive parser path.
rules.emitted_code: The outer callee expands and the copy retains inner calls. parsecommand retains five recursive calls in the oracle.
rules.counter_example: Genuinely separate units never inline across the object boundary. A recursive call is eligible for one expansion.
rules.reference: docs/FINDINGS.md / oeprobe and oeunits (supersedes the early macro model)

rules.rule: Owned static data and prior runtime address computation can leave calls intact.
rules.trigger: Callee owns a literal, static local or initialized local array, or caller evaluates a dynamic address before the call within one expression.
rules.source_form: A GAME callee with a literal or sprite[i].owner = findlocator(...).
rules.emitted_code: Retains an ordinary CALL in the documented controls, even above the size threshold.
rules.counter_example: Parameter count, static linkage and forward definition alone do not veto inlining. Splitting an expression can change the result.
rules.reference: docs/FINDINGS.md / Inliner facts and oeprobe

rules.rule: Two inline copies of the same source need not use identical instructions.
rules.trigger: Caller liveness and uses extend across several calls to an eligible same-unit function.
rules.source_form: Six keytimerstuff() calls in timerhandler.
rules.emitted_code: At the first copy the byte-load prefix uses XOR EAX/MOV AL then XOR EDX/MOV DL. The fifth inline site uses EDX for consecutive loads then AND EDX,255.
rules.counter_example: The standalone body has its own prologue and allocation. On the getpackets example, changing one mask operand order altered an inline copy while the standalone match survived.
rules.reference: STRICT code at timerhandler 1:002c7 and 1:008ff; docs/FINDINGS.md / GAME NEAR round 2

rules.rule: The tested Watcom register call puts four integer arguments in EAX, EDX, EBX, ECX.
rules.trigger: An ordinary __watcall with six integer arguments and no custom pragma.
rules.source_form: sink(side(1), side(2), side(3), side(4), side(5), side(6)).
rules.emitted_code: Calls side(6), side(5), then side(4) to side(1). Pushes the first two results, moves the other results into ECX, EBX, EDX, and leaves the final result in EAX.
rules.counter_example: Unrelated computations can move between pushes. Variadic printf/open and #pragma aux functions use other arrangements.
rules.reference: probes.json / args; STRICT EGS call in spawn_blood

rules.rule: Variadic calls can use stack arguments with caller cleanup.
rules.trigger: The library call is variadic, even when the format or actual argument count is constant.
rules.source_form: open("FILE_ID.DIZ", O_RDWR | O_BINARY, S_IREAD) and printf(help_usage, argv[0]).
rules.emitted_code: Rightmost argument pushed first, pointer pushed last, CALL, ADD ESP,12 or ADD ESP,8.
rules.counter_example: Ordinary game calls store four integer arguments in registers and pass excess arguments on the stack.
rules.reference: STRICT index

rules.rule: A missing prototype keeps default promotions at the call site.
rules.trigger: Caller sees an old-style function declaration or implicit int; callee can be in another TU.
rules.source_form: extern int EGS(); as seen by PLAYER; extern int strget(); in PREMAP.
rules.emitted_code: Arguments are built/passed without the prototype’s narrowing conversions, and getscorename tests EAX for the declared int return. Its own narrow Boolean result is SETNE AL.
rules.counter_example: A prototype with short parameter emitted CWDE in the long-to-short fixture. Actual declarations vary by caller; wholesale old-style conversion lost matches.

examples.source_text: j = EGS(sect, sx, sy, old_sz, 0, 46, -16, 0, 0, sa, 32, 0, i, 4);

rules.reference: docs/FINDINGS.md / PLAYER follow-up, PREMAP/GAME round 3 and Unit-wide declaration experiment; probes.json / oldarg and narrowarg

rules.rule: Use counts can move one value ahead of others in allocation.
rules.trigger: A long-lived local or compiler temporary competes with other values for overlapping register homes.
rules.source_form: playmusic(ps[screenpeek].music) instead of a song local; stage a common tile sum in cacheit.
rules.emitted_code: Different conflict savings/order can change the selected colour and later spills. One known control stages a named long tile and gains a 1,968-byte STRICT function.
rules.counter_example: A move of source text that preserves backend conflict order can give byte-identical output across many trials.
rules.reference: docs/CG95.md / Validation and engine results; docs/FINDINGS.md / Allocator lever

rules.rule: Register preference on a savings tie depends on traversal, overlap and prior-use state.
rules.trigger: The allocator sorts conflicts by descending savings and visits eligible register masks in order.
rules.source_form: Check same-priority spills and local scope/declaration order. In calcwalls and hline, homes change with declaration order.
rules.emitted_code: The first equal-score eligible mask stays incumbent unless a challenger was already used and the incumbent was not. The gap sorter can reorder equal-priority records as other records cross them.
rules.counter_example: A fixed list such as “always EAX then EDX” cannot predict the winner. checkhitswitch is a two-byte near control at equal savings 564; changing visit order also changed its neighbour.
rules.reference: docs/CG95.md / Breakpoints and recovered decisions; docs/FINDINGS.md / Allocation ties and checkhitswitch follow-up

rules.rule: Home order depends on priority and address-taking; declaration order can break ties.
rules.trigger: Frame slots survive optimization. Trace home priority uses a flag and size; aliases of the same temp have an offset order.
rules.source_form: Address-take s in spawn or reorder equal-priority locals as in hline.
rules.emitted_code: Trace placed spawn’s address-taken s at its last local home ([esp+0x14]) across declarations tested. hline changes the relative homes of r and xr.
rules.counter_example: A variable may remain in registers or share a home, and different flags or lifetimes can override any declaration-order effect.
rules.reference: docs/CG95.md / stack home comparator; docs/FINDINGS.md / PREMAP/GAME round 3 and Engine round 4

rules.rule: One address-taken short receives a four-byte local slot in the matched frame.
rules.trigger: Watcom 9.5 GA game_oe and the exact moveweapons local layout.
rules.source_form: short distance; findplayer(i, (long *)&distance);
rules.emitted_code: Slot at ESP+0xc is written as a long while projectile branches compare its signed low word.
rules.counter_example: The recorded 4-byte array and union variants leave 17 differences. Writing a long through a pointer cast to a short object has undefined behavior in portable C.
rules.reference: docs/FINDINGS.md / ACTORS/PREMAP on gpt-6.2-astra

rules.rule: The shape of a pragma aux declaration affects scheduling and register allocation.
rules.trigger: An inline pragma supplies the string move and register parameter mapping.
rules.source_form: Ken’s copybuf form with parm [esi][edi][ecx], without a modify clause.
rules.emitted_code: REP MOVSD in movelava and compiler unrolling around it, reproducing the 1,248-byte function.
rules.counter_example: The manual unroll and later modify clause were different source models. klabs without a C prototype also gives a distinctive MOV AX/CWDE path.
rules.reference: docs/FINDINGS.md / Ken-Build ancestry and Allocator lever

rules.rule: An ordinary literal is addressed by relocation into the unit’s CONST pool and can be reused.
rules.trigger: Same literal bytes, same unit, ordinary duplicate-string setting.
rules.source_form: string_sink("the same text"); in two procedures.
rules.emitted_code: The fixture emits the same CONST relocation and folds the identical procedures to the same entry. Game open/printf sites push the literal address.
rules.counter_example: An explicit reuse_duplicate_strings pragma or moving a call across a TU boundary changes pooling. Trailing embedded NUL bytes can affect the pool.
rules.reference: docs/FINDINGS.md / Link layout rules, GAME is two objects and CONST residue; probes.json / string_a–c

rules.rule: String alignment padding can inherit compiler record-buffer contents.
rules.trigger: Alignment gaps in reused covered LEDATA records, especially in literal-heavy GAMEDEF and SOUNDS.
rules.source_form: Use the actual source literal and headers to reproduce the full CONST segment.
rules.emitted_code: Prior LEDATA record contents can survive in covered padding. A record-transition hole is zero-filled by the linker. DOS 9.5 gives zero in the seed bytes observed in the oracle.
rules.counter_example: NT can seed the buffer from heap residue. Splitting GAMEDEF into .inc files changed about 50 bytes under DOS. Apogee 10.0 uses different residue in some pools.
rules.reference: docs/CONST_RESIDUE.md and docs/FINDINGS.md / Canonical DOS host

rules.rule: Watcom 10.0 CONST residue can come from the reused source-read buffer.
rules.trigger: A covered alignment gap in an Apogee unit after an include read or different predecessor unit.
rules.source_form: Unchanged source with the recorded guest include and source paths.
rules.emitted_code: Source offset model 4096*chunk+2153-round_up_4(DOS path length) predicts seven held-out offsets. Predecessor BLASTOLD reproduces some residue in MUSIC and FX_MAN.
rules.counter_example: No tested build reproduced all nine remaining pools. Exact 10.0 header versions and make order remain open.
rules.reference: docs/FINDINGS.md / Watcom 10.0 on the DOS host and Watcom 10.0 CONST residue solver

rules.rule: Watcom orders BSS by size buckets and declaration-slot and identifier-hash rules.
rules.trigger: File-scope uninitialized definitions; emitted allocation is sensitive to a rename or a new declaration.
rules.source_form: Same variables with reordered declarations; a far pointer or double under -ot can alter segment alignment.
rules.emitted_code: 9.5 rule uses newest 22-slot page first and ascending 12-bit identifier hash modulo 211, with type alignment under -ot and witnessed paragraph alignment for double/far function pointer. 10.0 uses its separately calibrated 25-slot/%241 model.
rules.counter_example: Using the 9.5 rule for the 10.0 calibration predicted 38/163; the calibrated 10.0 model predicted 163/163.
rules.reference: docs/BSS_LAYOUT.md; docs/FINDINGS.md / Compile environment, Link layout rules and Watcom 10.0 GA _BSS rule

rules.rule: Volatile keeps independent accesses and can affect operand selection.
rules.trigger: A repeated read or write to the same visible volatile object in one expression or block.
rules.source_form: return vol + vol; vol = 1; vol = 2; if (BLASTER_SoundPlaying || BLASTER_SoundRecording).
rules.emitted_code: The first fixture uses MOV and ADD from memory (two reads), while the nonvolatile version loads once and doubles the register. Both volatile stores survive. Both modes select a genuine word access for volatile short promotion.
rules.counter_example: Engine/multi also keep both nonvolatile stores in this fixture, whereas game_oe/audiolib keep only the second. A memory operand alone cannot identify volatile.
rules.reference: probes.json / readvolatile, storevolatile and widenvolatile; STRICT volatile uses

rules.rule: A simple global register-order rule is unlikely to explain the remaining ties.
rules.trigger: A function has a late alternate assignment with equal apparent costs in the disassembly.
rules.source_form: Compare neighbouring named and anonymous live ranges before editing the first differing operand.
rules.emitted_code: A local lifetime change may reproduce a tie by reordering the global conflict list. A controlled winning edit still needs a new strict verification.
rules.counter_example: The 150-trial permutation sweeps did not resolve the closest remaining ties; the trace establishes conditional preferences instead of a universal ranking.
rules.reference: docs/CG95.md; docs/FINDINGS.md / First tools/permute sweep
